events.reason: Postpartum follow-up; cough, night sweats, weight loss

documents.title: Obstetrics & Gynecology — Postpartum Follow-up
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRICS & GYNECOLOGY — clinic note, date of service 2023-02-07, addendum 2023-02-09
Faxed to primary care; PCP called directly 2/9.

29 y/o P1, about 4.5 months postpartum after SVD 9/26/22, here for a follow-up visit. She reports a cough for the past 3 weeks that will not go away, drenching sweats at night, and she has lost 5 kg over the same 3 weeks without trying. Has mild persistent asthma; albuterol has not changed the cough. She came to the US from a country where TB is common, about 5 years ago.

T 38.2 C. RR 22. SpO2 97% on room air.
Thin, tired-appearing. Crackles heard at both lung fields. Breasts and abdomen unremarkable. Uterus involuted.

CBC and BMP drawn today: within normal limits.
Tuberculin skin test placed today.

ADDENDUM 2/9: TST read at 48 hours, 15 mm induration. Called PCP, who is seeing her today for chest imaging and sputum. Advised a mask around others in the meantime.

events.reason: Positive TST with cough, fever, night sweats

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Patchy airspace opacities in both upper lobes. No cavitation. No pleural effusion. No hilar or mediastinal widening. Heart size normal. Bones intact.
reports.conclusion: Patchy bilateral upper-lobe opacities without cavitation or effusion. In the setting of a positive TST, findings are suspicious for pulmonary tuberculosis; correlate with sputum.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen at end of day in the separate room, pt and staff in N95s.

OB called earlier: TST 15 mm today at 48h. Pt has had ~3 wks of cough, mostly dry, some mornings productive of a little whitish sputum, no blood. Night sweats soaking her shirt most nights. Down 5 kg. Fevers in the evenings. No chest pain. Asthma inhaler doesn't touch it. Came to the US 2018; no known TB contact she's aware of; no prior TST or IGRA she can remember. Nobody at home sick that she knows of.

Recent OB vitals 2/7 and today's reviewed. Thin, tired. No lymphadenopathy. Lungs: crackles heard on both sides, no wheeze. Heart RRR. No hepatosplenomegaly.

CXR today (read back same day): patchy opacities both upper lobes, no cavity, no effusion.

A/P
Suspected active pulmonary TB: positive TST, symptoms, fever, weight loss and upper-lobe opacities.
- Sputum x3 for AFB smear, NAAT and culture: first tonight/tomorrow AM at home with kit, then 2 more mornings. Instructions given.
- HIV test today; baseline LFTs.
- Home isolation until cleared: no lab, no campus, masks with anyone in the home, open windows, no visitors. Letter for her department.
- Reported to the local board of health today as suspected TB; referral to the public health TB clinic for treatment and contact evaluation.
- Asthma: albuterol prn.
I'll call her with results. Long talk, she is scared, mostly about the baby; told her the health department team will walk the household through screening.

documents.title: Call — Board of Health
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Public health nurse from the board of health returned our report. They have the case and will contact pt today to arrange the TB clinic intake. Sputum kits: pt dropped off specimen #1 this morning, #2 and #3 tomorrow and Monday. CXR report and visit note faxed to the TB clinic per their request.

documents.title: HIV test result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your HIV test from yesterday is negative. Liver tests are normal, which is a useful baseline for TB medicines. Still waiting on the sputum results; I'll call you as soon as they're in.

documents.title: Phone Call — Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with sputum results. Specimen 1 AFB smear positive 1+, NAAT positive for M. tuberculosis complex with no rifampin resistance mutation. Specimens 2 and 3 smear negative. Cultures pending (weeks). This confirms pulmonary TB. Discussed that it is curable with a 6-month course of pills and that the TB clinic will run treatment with daily observed doses. Intake already set for Thu 2/16. Continue home isolation until the clinic clears her. Board of health updated by phone. She asked about the baby; the TB clinic and pediatrics are already in touch with each other. Will check in by video in a couple of weeks.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (300 mg) by mouth daily, directly observed
Take 2 capsules (600 mg) by mouth daily on an empty stomach, directly observed
Take 2 tablets (1,000 mg) by mouth daily, directly observed
Take 2 tablets (800 mg) by mouth daily, directly observed
Take 1 tablet (25 mg) by mouth daily with isoniazid

documents.title: TB Clinic — Initial Evaluation
documents.author: public health TB clinic
documents.body:
PUBLIC HEALTH TUBERCULOSIS CLINIC — INTAKE
Date: 2023-02-16
To: referring primary care physician

Thank you for the referral. 29-year-old woman, 4.5 months postpartum, foreign-born (arrived 2018), with 4 weeks of cough, fevers, night sweats and 5 kg weight loss. TST 15 mm (2/9). CXR 2/9 bilateral upper-lobe patchy opacities without cavitation. Sputum AFB smear 1+ on specimen 1, negative x2; Xpert MTB detected, rifampin resistance not detected. HIV negative 2/9. Asthma, kidney stones. NKDA.

Exam: afebrile here today, thin; scattered crackles bilaterally. Visual acuity and color vision normal. Baseline hepatic panel normal.

Assessment: pulmonary tuberculosis, smear positive, presumed drug susceptible.

Plan (weight-based dosing):
- Isoniazid 300 mg daily
- Rifampin 600 mg daily
- Pyrazinamide 1,000 mg daily
- Ethambutol 800 mg daily
- Pyridoxine 25 mg daily
Directly observed therapy by our nurses (video DOT on weekdays once established). Monthly visit with symptom review, weight, hepatic panel; monthly vision checks while on ethambutol.
Counseled: orange discoloration of urine and tears from rifampin, no alcohol, report nausea, jaundice, abdominal pain, rash, numbness or vision changes. Rifampin interacts with many drugs; check with us before any new prescription.
Home isolation continues; we will release her once she has 3 negative smears and clinical improvement on treatment.
Contact investigation of the household and lab coworkers is under way by our team.

Cultures and susceptibility pending.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt at home.

Two weeks into 4-drug TB therapy via the TB clinic, DOT by video. No fevers for about a week. Sweats much less. Cough still there but softer. Appetite starting to come back. Some queasiness if she takes the pills without food; the clinic told her to take them at bedtime with a snack, which helps. Urine orange as expected. No yellow eyes, rash, numbness or vision change. Not drinking alcohol. Asthma fine.

A/P: Pulmonary TB on RIPE + B6, tolerating. TB clinic managing monitoring; I'm getting their notes. Reminded her that rifampin interacts with many medicines, so anything new goes past the clinic. Will see in person once out of isolation.

results.text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex isolated. Susceptible to isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol.

documents.title: TB Clinic — Monthly Visit
documents.author: public health TB clinic
documents.body:
TB CLINIC — month 1 visit, 2023-03-22

Culture from 2/10 grew M. tuberculosis complex, pansusceptible (INH, RIF, PZA, EMB). Ethambutol discontinued today.

Symptoms: afebrile since late February; cough occasional; sweats resolved; appetite good. Weight up modestly from intake. DOT adherence 100%.

Sputum smears negative x3 since early March. Released from home isolation as of today; may return to campus and lab.

Hepatic panel normal. Vision unchanged.

Continue isoniazid 300, rifampin 600, pyrazinamide 1,000, pyridoxine 25 daily. Next visit one month, with 2-month sputum culture.

events.reason: TB follow-up, end of intensive phase

documents.title: TB Clinic — Monthly Visit
documents.author: public health TB clinic
documents.body:
TB CLINIC — month 2 visit, 2023-04-19

Two months of intensive-phase therapy completed. Asymptomatic apart from a rare cough. Hepatic panel normal.

Sputum culture collected at 2 months (3/29): no growth at final read.

Plan: stop pyrazinamide. Continuation phase isoniazid 300 mg + rifampin 600 mg daily with pyridoxine 25 mg for 4 more months, anticipated completion mid-August. Monthly visits continue.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First in-person since February. Continuation phase INH/RIF/B6, TB clinic notes through April reviewed (pansusceptible, 2-mo culture negative, PZA stopped). Feels 'like herself again.' Weight coming back. No cough most days. Back in the lab full time, writing up a chapter. Spring pollen bothering her eyes and nose; using albuterol about once a week on runs, which she's restarted at 2-3 miles.

Exam: well. Lungs clear. No icterus. Heart RRR.

A/P
1. Pulmonary TB, continuation phase. Doing well. TB clinic monitoring LFTs.
2. Mild persistent asthma: albuterol prn.
3. Allergic rhinitis: symptomatic, saline rinses; she'd like to avoid adding pills right now with the TB meds.
Physical in the fall.

documents.title: TB Clinic Visit Summary
documents.author: public health TB clinic
documents.body: TB clinic month 4 summary (visit 2023-06-19): on isoniazid/rifampin/pyridoxine, DOT adherence complete, no symptoms or side effects. Hepatic panel normal. Weight stable. Next visit 7/17.

documents.title: TB Clinic Visit Summary
documents.author: public health TB clinic
documents.body: TB clinic month 5 summary (visit 2023-07-17): continuation phase isoniazid/rifampin/pyridoxine, all doses observed. Feels well, no cough. Hepatic panel normal. Planned completion 8/17 with end-of-treatment chest film.

conditions.label: Personal history of tuberculosis
conditions.note: pulmonary, drug-susceptible; 6 months of therapy completed 2023-08-17

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Lungs are clear. The previously seen upper-lobe opacities have resolved. No effusion. Cardiomediastinal silhouette normal.
reports.conclusion: Clear lungs; interval resolution of prior bilateral upper-lobe opacities.

documents.title: TB Clinic — Completion of Therapy
documents.author: public health TB clinic
documents.body:
PUBLIC HEALTH TB CLINIC — COMPLETION OF THERAPY
To: primary care physician

Your patient completed treatment for drug-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis today, 2023-08-17: 2 months of isoniazid, rifampin and pyrazinamide (ethambutol for the first 5 weeks, until susceptibilities returned) followed by 4 months of isoniazid and rifampin, all with pyridoxine. 26 weeks, every dose observed.

Course: afebrile and smear-negative by early March; 2-month culture no growth. Hepatic panels normal throughout. No adverse effects.

End-of-treatment chest x-ray today: clear, with resolution of the upper-lobe opacities.

Weight back up since intake.

All TB medications stopped. She is considered cured. No routine follow-up imaging needed. Please re-evaluate for TB if she develops cough lasting more than 3 weeks, fevers, night sweats or weight loss. She has a copy of her treatment record. Household contact evaluations are complete.

Case closed with the health department.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

30F. What a year. Finished TB treatment 8/17, completion letter in chart: cured, CXR clear. Feels well, no cough, no sweats, weight back. Running 3-4 miles a few times a week. Fifth year of the PhD, deep in experiments. Child's care continues with pediatrics. Sleep better.

Asthma: albuterol maybe 2-3 times a month, mostly with runs in cold or high pollen. No nights. No ED visits this year.
Stones: none since joining. Drinks a big bottle of water at the lab.
Rhinitis: spring/late summer, tolerable.
No alcohol since the pregnancy; plans to keep it that way for now.

Meds: albuterol prn. Allergies: dust mites, pollen; NKDA.

PHQ-2: 1.

Exam: Well. BMI normal. HEENT normal, mild nasal mucosal pallor. Neck no LAD. Lungs clear. Heart RRR no murmur. Abd soft, NT. Skin normal. Ext no edema.

A/P
- Personal history of treated pulmonary TB: no further testing needed; future TSTs/IGRAs will stay positive and aren't useful; CXR + symptoms if ever needed.
- Mild persistent asthma: albuterol prn.
- Recurrent nephrolithiasis: quiet. Hydration.
- Allergic rhinitis due to pollen.
- HM: Pap due next year (age 30, co-test). Flu and COVID next month at nurse visit. HIV/HCV done in prenatal labs and HIV again in Feb, negative. CMP/CBC today.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your labs from the physical are all normal, including liver and kidney tests and blood counts. Nice to see everything back to baseline after the TB treatment.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (quadrivalent) in R deltoid and 2023-24 COVID (Pfizer) in L deltoid. No contraindications, feels well. Observed 15 minutes, fine. Records updated.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Malee, we missed you at your appointment yesterday at 2:00. Would you like to reschedule? Reply here or call the office.

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: So sorry!! I was stuck in the lab with a time-sensitive experiment and completely forgot. I'm doing fine, just the usual spring sneezing and itchy eyes, inhaler maybe once a week. Honestly ok to just see the doctor at my physical in September unless she wants me in sooner?

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No problem at all, that sounds fine. September physical it is. If you start needing the albuterol more than twice a week or it wakes you at night, come in sooner.

reports.text: Liquid-based cervical cytology. Specimen adequate, transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL

31F, sixth year of the PhD, starting to write. Feeling well. Sorry again about April.
Asthma: a few puffs a month, a bit more in spring. No nights, no urgent visits.
No stones, no urinary sx. No cough, sweats or weight loss.
Running 3-4x/week. No alcohol. Never smoker.
PHQ-2 0.

Exam: Well. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Abd benign, no CVA tenderness. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal-appearing, Pap/HPV co-test obtained. Skin normal.

A/P
- Health maintenance: Pap + HPV today. Flu/COVID at nurse visit next month.
- Mild persistent asthma: albuterol prn, has refills.
- Recurrent nephrolithiasis: quiet.
- History of TB: asymptomatic.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap and HPV test are both normal. With a normal co-test, the next one is due in 5 years (2029).

documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pt in for 2024-25 flu (trivalent) and COVID (Moderna) vaccines. Screening neg. Flu L deltoid, COVID R deltoid. Tolerated without issue, left after observation.
